docs.text: Looking up records in a Boost.MultiIndex container ¶ The problem ¶ Boost.MultiIndex keeps records in one container and gives you several indices over them: ordered, hashed, random access. Each index has a tag, a type that names it. To use an index you get it by its tag, search, and compare the result with end() : const auto& index = container.get<by_name>(); if (const auto it = index.find("user"); it != index.end()) { // found: use *it } else { // not found } This is correct, but every lookup repeats the same steps, and a missing record is handled in a different way in every place. A project with many containers ends up with many copies of the same few lines. Changing a record has its own trap. index.modify(it, modifier) returns false if the changed record breaks a unique index, and then the record is erased from the container . Nothing in the call says so. What the library does ¶ multi_index_lookup::container_extended_t is your Boost.MultiIndex container plus a few lookup functions. You inherit from it, so everything the container could do stays available. // by tag, a missing record is an empty optional const auto found = container.try_find_by<by_name>("user"); // by tag, a missing record calls the function you pass const auto& record = container.find_by_or_throw<by_name>("user", on_absent); // all records with the key for (const auto& record : container.equal_range_by<by_name>("user")) { /* ... */ } // change a record and learn what happened const auto result = container.try_find_by_and_modify<by_name>("user", modifier); What you get: One way to ask. Lookups take the tag as a template argument and return std::optional , a reference, or a range. A choice of what a missing record means. An empty result, a function that throws, or a pair of functions for "found" and "not found". Ranges. std::ranges::subrange of the index iterators, for one key or for a span of keys. An honest modify. The result says whether the record was absent, rejected or modified. With a rollback function a rejected record is not lost. It is a thin layer. It adds no data and no virtual functions, and it does not change how the container stores records. How this documentation is arranged ¶ Getting started : requirements, CMake and a first program. Your own container class : how the library is used in a project. A container becomes a class with its own name and its own methods, and Boost types stay hidden in detail .3. The guide: finding a record , finding ranges and modifying a record . Reference : every function, type and concept.

Getting started ¶ Requirements ¶ C++23. The library uses std::optional::transform and std::ranges::subrange . Boost.MultiIndex. If the target Boost::multi_index does not exist when the library is configured, the library fetches Boost itself, limited to MultiIndex. The library is header-only. The only target is the INTERFACE library multi_index_lookup::multi_index_lookup . CMake ¶ The library lives at github.com/goloveshin/multi_index_lookup . Fetch it with FetchContent : include(FetchContent) FetchContent_Declare( multi_index_lookup GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/goloveshin/multi_index_lookup.git GIT_TAG main ) FetchContent_MakeAvailable(multi_index_lookup) target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE multi_index_lookup::multi_index_lookup) Replace main with a release tag to pin a version. To use a local copy instead, replace GIT_REPOSITORY and GIT_TAG with SOURCE_DIR <path> . The library has an option MULTI_INDEX_LOOKUP_BUILD_TESTS . It builds the unit tests and the example of the library. It is ON only when multi_index_lookup is the top-level project, so a project that uses the library does not build them. You can set it yourself before FetchContent_MakeAvailable : set(MULTI_INDEX_LOOKUP_BUILD_TESTS OFF) If your project already provides Boost with MultiIndex, define the target Boost::multi_index before FetchContent_MakeAvailable and the library does not fetch another copy. The first program ¶ #include <multi_index_lookup.hpp> #include <boost/multi_index/member.hpp> #include <boost/multi_index/ordered_index.hpp> #include <boost/multi_index_container.hpp> #include <iostream> #include <stdexcept> #include <string> namespace bmi = boost::multi_index; struct record_t { int id; std::string name; }; struct by_id{}; using records_t = bmi::multi_index_container < record_t, bmi::indexed_by < bmi::ordered_unique < bmi::tag<by_id>, bmi::member<record_t, int, &record_t::id> > > >; using container_t = multi_index_lookup::container_extended_t<records_t>; int main() { const container_t container{ record_t{ 1, "one" }, record_t{ 2, "two" } }; // a missing record is an empty optional if (const auto found = container.try_find_by<by_id>(2)) { std::cout << "found: " << found->get().name << "
"; } if (!container.try_find_by<by_id>(9)) { std::cout << "9 is absent
"; } // a missing record calls the function, which must throw try { container.find_by_or_throw<by_id>(9, []{ throw std::runtime_error("no record 9"); }); } catch (const std::runtime_error& error) { std::cout << "error: " << error.what() << "
"; } } It prints: found: two 9 is absent error: no record 9 What happens here: records_t is an ordinary Boost.MultiIndex container with one index. The struct by_id is its tag. container_extended_t<records_t> is the same container with the lookup functions added. The constructors of records_t are inherited, so the container can be built from a list of records. try_find_by<by_id>(2) returns std::optional<std::reference_wrapper<const record_t>> . Use ->get() to reach the record. find_by_or_throw<by_id>(9, ...) returns the record, or calls the function when there is none. The function must throw; see Finding a record . In a real project you do not use container_extended_t<...> directly. You wrap it in a class of your own: see Your own container class .

docs.text: Finding a record ¶ All the examples use the container of example/aggregate_container.hpp : a container of aggregates with the index by_name (not unique) and the index by_vd (unique). Every lookup takes the tag of the index as a template argument and the key as the first argument: container.try_find_by<by_vd>(3); The key is passed to find of that index, so it can be anything the index accepts. What a missing record means ¶ The functions differ in what they do when there is no record. The name tells which: name a missing record try_find_* the result is an empty std::optional find_*_or_throw the function you pass is called, and it must throw find_*_and_do you pass two functions: one for found, one for not found try_find_by ¶ const auto found = container.try_find_by<by_vd>(3); if (found) { const auto& record = found->get(); } It returns std::optional<std::reference_wrapper<const record_t>> . The type is also available as container_t::record_ocrt . The reference points into the container, there is no copy. If the index is not unique, the result is one of the records with the key. To get all of them use equal_range_by . try_find_iterator_by ¶ const auto found = container.try_find_iterator_by<by_vd>(3); The same, but the result is std::optional of the iterator of the index by_vd . Use it when you need the position, not only the record: for example to erase the record or to pass it to modify . find_by_or_throw ¶ const auto& record = container.find_by_or_throw<by_vd>( 3, [&]{ throw std::runtime_error("no aggregate 3"); } ); It returns const record_t& . If there is no record, the function is called. Warning The function must throw . If it returns, the library throws std::bad_optional_access , because it has no record to return. The library does not choose the exception for you, so a project can throw its own type, with its own information. find_iterator_by_or_throw does the same and returns the iterator. find_by_and_do ¶ const std::string text = container.find_by_and_do<by_vd>( 3, // found [](const auto& index, const auto& iterator, const record_t& record) { return record.name; }, // not found [](const auto& index) { return std::string("no such aggregate"); } ); It calls one of the two functions and returns what it returned. and_then_func(index, iterator, record) is called when the record is found. index is the index chosen by the tag, iterator points to the record, record is the record. or_else_func(index) is called when it is not found. Both functions must return the same type. That type is the result of find_by_and_do . Both can return void . The names are the same as and_then and or_else of std::optional . to_non_const ¶ The records of a Boost.MultiIndex container are const . to_non_const removes const from a record that you found: auto& record = container_t::to_non_const(container.find_by_or_throw<by_vd>(3, on_absent)); record.is_root = false; It has three forms: for const record_t& , for std::reference_wrapper<const record_t> , and for the std::optional of it that try_find_by returns. Warning Change only the fields that no index uses as a key. If you change a key, the index is not updated and it breaks. To change a key use try_find_by_and_modify .

docs.text: Modifying a record ¶ The records of a Boost.MultiIndex container are const , because a key that changes under an index would break it. To change a record you ask the index to do it: index.modify(iterator, modifier) . The index takes the record out of its position, calls the modifier and puts the record back where the new keys say. The library finds the record by the key and does this for you, and reports what happened. What can go wrong ¶ Changing a record can make it clash with another one. For example, a unique index already has a record with the new key. Boost.MultiIndex cannot keep both, so modify returns false . What happens to the record depends on the form of modify : call on a clash modify(it, modifier) the record is erased from the container modify(it, modifier, rollback) rollback is called to restore the record, and the record stays If the modifier itself throws, Boost.MultiIndex erases the record and the exception goes on. The library has both forms. try_find_by_and_modify ¶ const auto result = container.try_find_by_and_modify<by_vd>( 3, [](record_t& record){ record.name = "orders"; } ); It finds the record by the key and calls the modifier with the record. The result is modify_result_et : result meaning absent there is no record with the key, nothing is changed modified the record is changed rejected the change broke an index, see below The enumeration is multi_index_lookup::modify_result_et . It is also available in the class as container_t::modify_result_et , so a class that derives from container_extended_t can write modify_result_et::absent . Warning With this form, rejected means that the record is gone . Boost.MultiIndex erased it. If that is not acceptable, use the form with the rollback function. With a rollback function ¶ const auto result = container.try_find_by_and_modify<by_vd>( 3, // the change [](record_t& record){ record.vd = 4; }, // return the record to the state before the change [](record_t& record){ record.vd = 3; } ); If the new vd is already taken, the rollback function returns the record to vd 3, and the record stays in the container. The result is rejected : the change was refused, and nothing is lost. The rollback function must really restore the record. If the indices are still broken after it, Boost.MultiIndex erases the record, as in the form without a rollback. The rollback function is called only for rejected . It is not called for absent and modified . find_by_and_modify ¶ Calls a function for each outcome that is not modified : container.find_by_and_modify<by_vd>( 3, // on_absent [&]{ throw std::runtime_error("no aggregate 3"); }, // on_rejected [&]{ throw std::runtime_error("cannot change aggregate 3"); }, // the change [](record_t& record){ record.vd = 4; } ); on_absent() is called when there is no record. on_rejected() is called when the change was rejected. Nothing is called when the record is modified. Unlike find_by_or_throw , these functions do not have to throw. If they return, find_by_and_modify returns, and the caller can look at its own state. There is an overload with the rollback function as the last argument: container.find_by_and_modify<by_vd>( 3, on_absent, on_rejected, [](record_t& record){ record.vd = 4; }, [](record_t& record){ record.vd = 3; } ); With it, a rejected change leaves the record in the container, and on_rejected is called after the rollback. Which form to use ¶ If the changed fields are not keys of a unique index, a change cannot be rejected. The simple form is enough. If a change can clash with another record and losing the record is a bug, use a rollback function. If a clash means that the record must go, the form without a rollback does exactly that, and rejected tells you that it happened. Changing a field that is not a key ¶ When no index uses the field as a key, you do not need modify . See to_non_const in Finding a record .

docs.text: Finding ranges ¶ An index that is not unique can have many records with one key. An ordered index also keeps the records sorted, so records with keys from a span of values are next to each other. The library gives both as a range. A range is std::ranges::subrange of the iterators of the index. It does not copy the records, and an empty range means that nothing was found. equal_range_by ¶ All the records with the key: for (const auto& record : container.equal_range_by<by_name>("user")) { // every aggregate named "user" } If there are no such records, the range is empty. There is no "absent" state, so the function does not start with try_ . The type of the range is container_t::range_by_t<by_name, std::string> for the key type std::string . It is the type to use in a signature when you need to write it: using range_t = container_t::range_by_t<by_name, std::string>; range_between ¶ The records with the keys from lower to upper , both included : // the records of the index by_vd with the vd 1, 2 and 3 const auto range = container.range_between<by_vd>(1, 3); It works from lower_bound(lower) to upper_bound(upper) of the index. If no key is between, or if lower is greater than upper , the range is empty. For a composite key ( composite_key of Boost.MultiIndex) the bounds can be partial tuples. This is how a range of "all the records of this parent" is taken. find_range_by_and_do ¶ Like find_by_and_do , for a range: const std::size_t count = container.find_range_by_and_do<by_name>( "user", // the range is not empty [](const auto& index, auto& range) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(std::ranges::distance(range)); }, // the range is empty [](const auto& index) { return std::size_t{ 0 }; } ); and_then_func(index, range) is called when the range is not empty. range is a non-const lvalue. or_else_func(index) is called when it is empty. Both functions must return the same type, and it is the result of find_range_by_and_do . Ranges and algorithms ¶ The result is a standard range, so it works with the standard library and with range libraries: const auto range = container.equal_range_by<by_name>("user"); const bool is_any = !range.empty(); const auto count = std::ranges::distance(range); Note A range is a view. It refers to the container, so do not keep it after the container changes. Erasing or modifying a record that the range covers can make the range invalid.
docs.title: Finding ranges

docs.text: The records with the keys from lower to upper , both included : // the records of the index by_vd with the vd 1, 2 and 3 const auto range = container.range_between<by_vd>(1, 3); It works from lower_bound(lower) to upper_bound(upper) of the index. If no key is between, or if lower is greater than upper , the range is empty. For a composite key ( composite_key of Boost.MultiIndex) the bounds can be partial tuples. This is how a range of "all the records of this parent" is taken.
docs.title: range_between

docs.text: Like find_by_and_do , for a range: const std::size_t count = container.find_range_by_and_do<by_name>( "user", // the range is not empty [](const auto& index, auto& range) { return static_cast<std::size_t>(std::ranges::distance(range)); }, // the range is empty [](const auto& index) { return std::size_t{ 0 }; } ); and_then_func(index, range) is called when the range is not empty. range is a non-const lvalue. or_else_func(index) is called when it is empty. Both functions must return the same type, and it is the result of find_range_by_and_do .
docs.title: find_range_by_and_do

docs.text: The result is a standard range, so it works with the standard library and with range libraries: const auto range = container.equal_range_by<by_name>("user"); const bool is_any = !range.empty(); const auto count = std::ranges::distance(range); Note A range is a view. It refers to the container, so do not keep it after the container changes. Erasing or modifying a record that the range covers can make the range invalid.

docs.text: Your own container class ¶ container_extended_t<...> is not meant to be used directly in a project. A container usually has a meaning: "aggregates by name", "places by id". The meaning deserves a name, and the code that uses the container should not see Boost types. This page shows the organization that the library is designed for. It is the recommended way to use it. The full code, which builds and runs, is the example/ directory of the library. The layout ¶ Every container lives in its own namespace and has the same three parts: detail : the record, the keys and the raw Boost.MultiIndex container. A class container_t that derives from container_extended_t<detail::container_t> . Methods of that class that give the lookups names from the domain. This is aggregate_container of the example. It keeps aggregates by name, and one of them is the root: // aggregates by name, including the root one namespace example::aggregate_container { namespace detail { struct record_t { std::string name; int vd; bool is_root; }; // the key of the index by name: a field extraction struct by_name { using result_type = const std::string&; result_type operator()(const record_t& record) const { return record.name; } }; struct by_vd{}; using namespace boost::multi_index; using container_t = multi_index_container < record_t, indexed_by < random_access<>, ordered_non_unique < tag<by_name>, by_name >, ordered_unique < tag<by_vd>, member<record_t, int, &record_t::vd> > > >; }// namespace detail class container_t : public multi_index_lookup::container_extended_t<detail::container_t> { public: void add(const std::string& name, const int vd, const bool is_root) { push_back(detail::record_t{ .name = name, .vd = vd, .is_root = is_root }); } // ... template <typename ... Args> decltype(auto) try_find_range_by_name(Args&& ... args) const { return equal_range_by<detail::by_name>(std::forward<Args>(args)...); } }; }// namespace example::aggregate_container Why it is arranged this way ¶ detail keeps Boost out of sight ¶ The record, the key extractors and the raw container are in namespace detail . The line using namespace boost::multi_index; is also there, so the long Boost names are short inside detail and never leak to the code that includes the header. The code that uses aggregate_container::container_t never writes multi_index_container , indexed_by or tag . The key is a type, and it is also the tag ¶ by_name is a function object that takes a record and returns the key. This is called field extraction . The same type is passed to tag<by_name> , so the type that extracts the key is also the name of the index: ordered_non_unique < tag<by_name>, // the name of the index by_name // how to get the key from a record > Later the tag is what you give to the library: equal_range_by<detail::by_name>(...) . A key can be more than a field. by_name could return a computed value or a tuple. For the simple case Boost.MultiIndex has the standard member<...> ; the example uses it for the index by_vd , where the tag is an empty struct. container_t is a class, not an alias ¶ class container_t : public multi_index_lookup::container_extended_t<detail::container_t> A class lets you add methods that mean something: add , root , rename . Everything of the Boost container and of container_extended_t stays public, so inside the class (and outside) you can still iterate over the records, call push_back and so on. The name container_t can be the same in every namespace. The namespace tells the containers apart: aggregate_container::container_t , order_container::container_t . A method gives a lookup its name ¶ template <typename ... Args> decltype(auto) try_find_range_by_name(Args&& ... args) const { return equal_range_by<detail::by_name>(std::forward<Args>(args)...); } The caller writes aggregates.try_find_range_by_name(name) . It does not know about tags. The forwarding keeps the lookup open to every key the index accepts, including tuples for composite keys. The class can have any other methods. For example, it finds the root aggregate and throws when there is none: const detail::record_t& root() const { for (const auto& record : *this) { if (record.is_root) { return record; } } throw std::runtime_error("cannot find root aggregate"); } A lookup that throws ¶ A method can report a missing record in the way the project wants. The library does not choose the exception type, the project does: const detail::record_t& find_by_vd(const int vd) const { return find_by_or_throw<detail::by_vd>( vd, [vd] { throw std::runtime_error("cannot find aggregate " + std::to_string(vd)); } ); } find_by_or_throw gets the function that reports the problem, and the function must throw. A project with its own exception type throws it here, with its own information. See Finding a record . A lookup that handles both outcomes ¶ When a missing record is not an error, find_by_and_do takes two functions: std::string describe(const int vd) const { return find_by_and_do<detail::by_vd>( vd, [](const auto&, const auto&, const detail::record_t& record) { return record.name + (record.is_root ? " (root)" : ""); }, [](const auto&) { return std::string("no such aggregate"); } ); } The same is available for ranges with find_range_by_and_do . See Finding ranges . A modification with a rollback ¶ The modification is written once in the class, and the callers pass only what to change. renumber changes the key vd of a unique index, so the new value may be taken. The rollback function keeps the record in that case: // the new vd may be taken: then the record stays as it was modify_result_et renumber(const int vd, const int new_vd) { return try_find_by_and_modify<detail::by_vd>( vd, [new_vd](detail::record_t& record){ record.vd = new_vd; }, [vd](detail::record_t& record){ record.vd = vd; } ); } modify_result_et is available in the class without a qualification. See Modifying a record . Summary ¶ Part Where What it holds record, keys, raw container namespace detail everything that is Boost.MultiIndex the class container_t the namespace of the container the public name and the methods of the domain lookup methods the class one name per lookup, forwarding to the library
